identity.mechanic:
**The River.** Your board, read as one stream along the touching zigzag. It runs from the mouth (F4) upstream to the **Source** (F1): F4 → B3 → F3 → B2 → F2 → B1 → F1. *Upstream* and *downstream* mean along that order. In card text, *Salmon* means any unit of this tribe, the heron Bailiff included. **Home and Spawn.** The first Salmon each fight to leap into the Source comes **Home**. At the next Start of Turn it **Spawns**:
1. **Gift:** each unit touching it gains +1/+1 permanently for each Stamp it has (any tribe).
2. Its **Spent:** effect, if it has one.
3. It is spent: an Alevin (Created) takes its slot with half its Stamps.

keywords.name: Leap
keywords.text: In a fight, when the next slot upstream of this empties (its unit dies, leaps or drifts away), this leaps into it. Its first leap each fight stamps its passport: it gains a **Stamp**, a permanent counter. A gap that was already there pulls nobody, so the run has to be unbroken. One death near the head pulls the whole run up a step, and the units swap between rows as they go.

keywords.name: Home and Spawn
keywords.text:
The first Salmon each fight to leap into the Source comes **Home**. At the next Start of Turn it **Spawns**:
1. **Gift:** each unit touching it gains +1/+1 permanently for each Stamp it has (any tribe).
2. Its **Spent:** effect, if it has one.
3. It is spent: an Alevin (Created) takes its slot with half its Stamps.

identity.plays: Each Recruit Phase you set the river. You choose who sits at the Source to die first and open the way, who waits at B1 as the next pilgrim home, which veterans stay far downstream to keep collecting Stamps, and which neighbours of the next pilgrim will catch its Gift. In the fight the run climbs in cascades, swapping rows as it goes, and those who move collect Stamps. Afterwards the one who made it home spends itself into a Gift and an Alevin. The tribe has two pulls that work against each other: keep fish on the road (Stamps grow) or send them home (spending pays now and feeds triples). The best boards do both, with different fish.

units.name: Brother Grilse
units.text: Once a fight, when this leaps, it gains +2/+1 this fight. *(Back after one winter, trying too hard.)*

units.name: Silver Smolt
units.text: When played: give another unit a Stamp, then +1/+1 permanently for each Stamp it has.

units.name: The Bailiff of the Weir
units.text: No Leap (a heron). Start of Turn: each Salmon touching this gains a Stamp. When sold: a Salmon touching this Spawns now.
units.golden: 6/6. Two Stamps each. When sold: up to two touching Salmon Spawn.

units.name: Little Jack Gravel
units.text: No Leap (never went to sea). Once a turn, when another of your Salmon Spawns, add an Alevin to your hand.

units.name: Old Kelt
units.text: Start of Combat: drift into the furthest empty slot downstream (the run leaps up behind it). Salmon that leap at Start of Combat gain +1 Attack this fight.

units.name: Sea Trout Ferrywife
units.golden: 6/8. Units within two steps along the river have Leap.

units.name: Reunion Cock
units.text: End of Turn: your other units with exactly as many Stamps as this gain +1/+2 permanently. *(Year-class meets year-class.)*

units.name: Falls-Leaper
units.text: Whenever another of your units leaps, this gains +1 Attack this fight.

units.name: The Faroes Bore
units.text: Start of Turn: tell a random other Salmon about the Far Feeding. It gains +1/+1 permanently for each Stamp this has.

units.name: Sea-Fed Hen
units.text: Spent: your units that aren't Salmon gain +1/+1 permanently for each Stamp this had.

units.name: Pebble-Carrying Hen
units.text: When one of your Salmon Spawns, its Alevin keeps all its Stamps, not half.

units.name: Second-Run Hen
units.text: Once a turn, when another of your Salmon Spawns, its Gift and Spent effect happen again.

units.name: Warden of the Hazel Well
units.text: Your Salmon can come Home any number of times a fight. Whenever one comes Home, your units gain +1/+1 permanently.

units.name: Captain Kype
units.text: Has Cleave while it has 3 or more Stamps. Twice a fight, when this leaps, it attacks at once. *(First at every leap.)*

units.name: Claw-Marked Cock
units.text: Whenever this leaps into the front row, it gains Shield and +2/+2 this fight. *(He has met the bears.)*

units.name: Mother Redd
units.text: Your Salmon aren't spent when they Spawn: they stay, with their Stamps, and their Alevin goes to your hand instead. *(Third run. She'll tell you.)*

units.name: Old Bradán
units.text: Start of Combat: your other Salmon give their Gifts and Spent effects as if they Spawned, but what they give lasts only this fight. They aren't spent. *(He answers everything, then forgets.)*

units.name: The Salmon of Llyn Llyw
units.text: Your other units have Leap. Your units have +1/+1 for each Stamp they have. *(Oldest of animals; carried Arthur's men.)*

builds.name: The Homecoming (spend for value)
builds.text: Old Kelt goes at the Source with one gap at the mouth. At Start of Combat he drifts down and the whole run leaps up a step, which gives every fish a Stamp and sends one home every fight. Queue fish with Spent text at B1 (Sea-Fed Hen) and back them with Second-Run Hen. The Bailiff, when sold, is a spawn outlet on demand. Little Jack Gravel turns each Spawn into a spare Alevin, and three Alevins make a golden, which Discovers. Warden of the Hazel Well lifts the one-a-fight limit. Mother Redd stops the run from shrinking, and Bradán replays every Gift inside the fight.

builds.name: The Long Road (never go home)
builds.text: Block the way home: put a non-Leap unit (Jack, the Bailiff, or another tribe's tank) at B1, so nobody reaches the Source. The fish just collect Stamps. The Bailiff stamps his neighbours, Silver Smolt adds Stamps and turns them into stats, and the Reunion Cock pays out when the year-classes line up. Because the whole run leaps together, the classes stay lined up on their own. The Faroes Bore turns one veteran's Stamps into growth for the others, and Captain Kype turns red (Cleave) at 3. Llyn Llyw is the payoff: every Stamp on every unit becomes stats. Pebble-Carrying Hen lets you still spawn now and then without losing a line's Stamps.

builds.name: The Cascade (in-fight leaping)
builds.text: A fragile unit sits at the Source and a long, unbroken run sits behind it. Every death near the head pulls six fish at once. Falls-Leaper counts every leap, Brother Grilse and Claw-Marked Cock power up when they leap (the Cock gains Shield each time he lands in the front row), and Captain Kype makes extra attacks. Old Kelt starts a cascade before the first blow.

builds.name: Feeding the Forest (Salmon as support)
builds.text: Another tribe's carry sits at the Source or at F2, where it touches B1, so it catches the Gift from every fish that comes home. Sea-Fed Hen feeds all non-Salmon at once. Sea Trout Ferrywife and Llyn Llyw put other tribes on the road, so they collect Stamps that Smolt, Reunion Cock and Llyn Llyw read.

builds.name: Lobby mixes
builds.text:
- **Birds:** a sold Bird's Nest Egg (0/1) at the Source dies to the first hit, which means a homecoming almost every fight without Kelt.
- **Oozes:** Alevins are free food for Eat, and stamped Alevins are meaty. A Belly's release takes the dying Ooze's slot, so the slot never empties and the run behind it is held back on purpose.
- **Bog folk:** a Mire unit at the Source holds for a long time, so homecomings come late. That suits the Long Road.
- **Hunters:** with Leap from the Ferrywife, a Hunter's "across" changes as it climbs, so it can chase a new quarry.
- **Hedgerow:** recruit slots come back after the fight, so turns-in-slot clocks survive leaping. The Gift makes F1/F2 a second growth spot next to Pass's rightmost unit.
- **Fairies:** a fish that leaps onto a Ring slot raises the rules question below.

risks: **Losing a fish you didn't mean to lose.** A Spawn is automatic. The UI has to mark the next pilgrim (the Leap unit at B1) and preview its Gift, or players will feel robbed. If that isn't enough, make Spawn optional at Start of Turn, with a refusal keeping the Home mark one more turn.
**Alevins triple on the board.** A third Alevin turns into a golden at once and leaves gaps in the run halfway through recruiting. That's readable but surprising, so it needs a clear animation.

**Alevin flood.** Mother Redd, Jack and the Warden together could make a golden Alevin, and so a Discover, almost every turn late in the game. That's an economy loop, not a stat loop. If it runs away, Mother Redd's Alevins could go to the board's nearest empty slot instead of the hand.

**Old Kelt is binary.** With one empty slot he is excellent: a Stamp for every fish in the run and a guaranteed homecoming. With a full board he does nothing. Watch whether giving up a slot is the right price.
**Bookkeeping.** Every unit carries a Stamp count, and the Reunion Cock's "exactly as many" needs Stamps visible on the board at all times.

**Rules to settle:** When Bradán and Kelt both act at Start of Combat, reading order decides whose positions the Gifts use. Does a fish that leaps onto a Fairy Ring slot gain the Ring in that fight? Proposal: no, Rings count only where a unit starts the fight. Leaps move front-row units into the back row, so the front can empty early and expose the back row. That's intended, but it interacts with Swoop.
**The Long Road depends on blocking B1.** If players find homecoming always better, the Stamp cards fall behind. The Faroes Bore and Llyn Llyw are the levers to watch.

tier_check.note: Alevin is a small seed (3 body) that grows about +2 stats a fight (~0.5 body), close to the guide. Grilse is a 5-body tempo unit with about +3 in fight (~0.75), a little high but conditional.

Smolt gives about +8 once with 3 Stamps (1.3 bodies), on target. The Bailiff gives 2 Stamps a turn, worth whatever reads them. Jack gives a Created Alevin each turn, about a third of a triple, which is fair economy.

Reunion Cock gives 6–9 a turn (0.9–1.3), and Falls-Leaper +6–10 Attack in fight, both in range. Old Kelt breaks the guide upward on purpose: he gives a whole run a Stamp each fight, paid for with a board slot. The Ferrywife gives no stats itself; she is a pure enabler.

The Faroes Bore gives about 10 a turn at 5 Stamps (1.2) and Sea-Fed Hen 12–24 once, plus a lost body, both on target. Second-Run Hen doubles a 16–24 Spawn (up to ~2.5 bodies), above the guide on purpose as the tribe's first multiplier, capped at once a turn.

The Warden gives 14–42 a turn (1.2–3.5) and sets the direction. Kype makes two extra Cleave attacks (~2–3 bodies in fight), a little under the guide but repeatable. Claw-Marked Cock is tempo: up to three Shields and +6/+6 in a long cascade.

Mother Redd keeps a ~15-stat adult and repeats its Spent effect at each Spawn (2–4 bodies a turn, more with Spent cards), so she is a multiplier capstone. Bradán gives 80–120 in fight (6–8 bodies), at the top of the guide. Llyn Llyw gives 70–110 once (5–8) and then grows about 14 or more a turn. None of them feeds its own source: Stamps come from fights, the Bailiff and Smolt, never from stats.

rationale: **The fantasy came first:** the board is a river and the units are pilgrims climbing it. The touching zigzag already makes a single stream, so it became the River.
**Movement happens in fights.** Players move units freely while recruiting, so positions there can't be progress. Leap fires when the slot ahead empties.
**Gaps that are already there pull nobody.** Otherwise an early board of two units would send everyone home on turn 2.
**A Stamp counts the fights a fish has moved in.** One per fight keeps it readable and stops a stat flood. Each card decides what Stamps are worth.
**"First home each fight"** makes the next pilgrim predictable, so B1 becomes a decision each turn.
**The gift to the forest is the keyword itself.** The Gift goes to touching units of any tribe, and that is the main way the Run mixes with other tribes.
**The spent fish leaves an Alevin in its own slot:** the next run starts in the same gravel and the run stays unbroken. The Alevin is a pool unit, so spawning feeds triples.
**Old Kelt drifting seaward** is the seed's own image of making room for the run, and the cleanest guaranteed homecoming. He costs a board slot.
**Year-classes became a matching puzzle.** The whole run leaps together, so classes stay lined up until a Spawn or a Stamp-giver breaks them.
**Arthur's men carried by Llyn Llyw** became Leap for other tribes (the Ferrywife locally, Llyn Llyw everywhere), so Johnny can run anyone up the river.
**"Spending yourself" has two capstones:** Mother Redd removes the cost, and Bradán replays the reward and forgets it.

**Each named figure got the card its line suggests:** Kype is first at the leap, Jack sneaks a spare Alevin, the Bailiff stamps passports and eats one when sold, and the Faroes Bore won't stop talking.
